items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Well in Chicago I was playing with a boy named Francois Mosley... And I was in the twenties and he was playing tuba with us.

ctx.x: Well I don't know about here. Well in Chicago I was playing with a boy named Francois Mosley and the other fella named William Hilliard. And I was in the twenties and he was playing tuba with us. And he played so, man you thought it was a bass violin. He didn't play no louder than the orchestra played. Except that tuba right down there. But William Hilliard, they called him Bill Hilliard.
That's right, he's on the record with you I think. Yeah, yeah.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Francois was on the drums. And we had Al Wins a lot of different times... I was on the trumpet.

ctx.x: But we had a lovely band at the Golden Lill in Chicago. We had five years, like one spot. A boy named little Francois Mosley had the band, and the place caught a fire on a Saturday night. That's how we got out of job there. But we would have been there, I guess, for 10 years. That was a nice job.
Who was in the band ready to go to the world?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. Charlie Ducasse, myself, Fred Reed on piano.

ctx.x: Oh, I wanted to ask you about Frankie Halfpaint Jackson. You made a record with him, huh? Oh, yeah. I made a record with him. You remember who was in that band?

Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. Charlie Ducasse, myself, Fred Reed on piano. And Charlie Ducasse on guitar and that boy, Lil Sax on tenor. Fred Howard on alto. He played alto on clarinet. And what else? Fred on piano, me on trumpet. Al Wynn on trombone. Al Wynn. I got a letter from him the other day. Little Sax's name is what? Robert Crowder. Everybody called him. You know who he was, Kenta? Y'all didn't know Cecil. He used to play with Earl Hein.
